# Migrating from React Email
## [Component map](https://maizzle.com/docs/migrate/react-email#component-map)
Maizzle has almost 100% parity with React Email's core components, making it very easy to migrate: keep using the same component names, just switch to Vue SFCs instead of JSX.

## [Styling](https://maizzle.com/docs/migrate/react-email#styling)
With Maizzle, you typically use Tailwind, but can also use style objects or inline CSS.

React EmailMaizzle

## [Rendering](https://maizzle.com/docs/migrate/react-email#rendering)
React Email's `render()` becomes Maizzle's [`render()`](https://maizzle.com/docs/api/utilities#render):

React EmailMaizzle

```ts
import { render } from 'react-email'
import { WelcomeEmail } from './emails/welcome'

const html = await render(<WelcomeEmail name="Alex" />)
```

```ts
import { render } from '@maizzle/framework'

const { html } = await render('emails/welcome.vue', config?)
```

`render()` runs the full pipeline — SSR, CSS inlining, transformers, doctype — and returns `html` plus (optionally) `plaintext`.

## Quick Comparison
| Tool | Best For | Starting Price | Free Tier | Dev Features |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| React Email | React teams | Free | Yes | React components, TypeScript, hot reload |
| Maizzle | Tailwind-based email | Free | Yes | Tailwind CSS, build pipeline, components |
| Resend | Developer-first sending | $20/mo | Yes | React Email native, API-first |

## The Best Developer-Focused Email Tools
### 3. React Email - Modern Component Approach
React Email brings component-based development to email templates.

```
import { Html, Button, Text, Section } from '@react-email/components';

export function WelcomeEmail({ userName }) {
  return (
    <Html>
      <Section>
        <Text>Hello {userName},</Text>
        <Text>Thanks for signing up!</Text>
        <Button href="https://example.com/dashboard">
          Go to Dashboard
        </Button>
      </Section>
    </Html>
  );
}
```

But you can use React Email with any sending service by rendering to HTML.

## Developer Tool Comparison
| Tool | Approach | Learning Curve | Build Integration | Active Development |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| React Email | React components | Medium | Excellent | Yes |
| Maizzle | Tailwind-based | Low (if you know Tailwind) | Excellent | Yes |

## Choosing the Right Tool
**If your team lives in React:** React Email.

**If you love Tailwind:** Maizzle.

web.description:
# 20 Best Free Email Templates (HTML + React) 2026
- **Best React framework:** [React Email](https://adminlte.io/blog/free-email-templates/#react-email) — 18k stars, built by Resend, templates for Stripe/Vercel/Notion
- **Best with Tailwind:** [Maizzle](https://adminlte.io/blog/free-email-templates/#maizzle) — Write Tailwind CSS, get inlined email HTML

## React & JSX Email Frameworks
If you’re already building with React, these frameworks let you write emails using the same component patterns you use for your web app. They compile JSX to cross-client compatible HTML at build time.

## 1. React Email
![React Email - Templates page showing AWS, GitHub, Apple, Nike email recreations](https://adminlte.io/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/react-email-templates.png)

React + TypeScript

Free / MIT

Best for: React Teams Building Transactional Email

**Why we like it:** React Email doesn’t just give you components — it ships with production-quality recreations of emails from Stripe, Vercel, Notion, Linear, AWS, Apple, and Nike. You can clone and customize real-world email designs from top companies.

**Editor’s Pick:** React Email is our top recommendation for any team already using React. The component library is excellent, the template gallery provides real-world starting points, and Resend’s backing means it’s actively maintained.

Built by the team behind Resend, React Email provides a set of components (`Html`, `Head`, `Section`, `Row`, `Column`, `Button`, `Img`) that render to cross-client HTML.

With 18k+ GitHub stars and active development, React Email has become the standard for React-based email development. The template gallery alone is worth bookmarking.

[GitHub](https://github.com/resend/react-email) [Templates](https://react.email/examples)

## 2. JSX Email
![JSX Email - JSX email framework with Tailwind CSS support](https://adminlte.io/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/jsx-email-framework.png)

JSX/TSX + Tailwind CSS

Free / MIT

Best for: Tailwind-First Email Development

**Why we like it:** JSX Email adds what React Email lacks — native Tailwind CSS support and a plugin system for inline CSS, minification, and Markdown rendering. If your codebase is Tailwind-first, this is the natural choice.

JSX Email is an alternative to React Email that focuses on developer experience and extensibility. The component API is similar, but it adds first-class Tailwind CSS support (classes compile to inline styles), a plugin architecture, and built-in Markdown rendering for content-heavy emails.

[GitHub](https://github.com/shellscape/jsx-email) [Website](https://jsx.email/)

## 3. Mailing
![Mailing - Build, test, and send emails with React](https://adminlte.io/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/mailing-react-email.png)

React + TypeScript + Next.js

It integrates with your Next.js app, provides a local preview server with hot reload, supports test sending to real inboxes, and handles transport via any email provider (Sendgrid, SES, Postmark, etc.).

## 4. MJML-React
Free / MIT

**Why we like it:** Combines the best of both worlds — React’s component model with MJML’s proven email rendering engine.

## 7. Maizzle
![Maizzle - Build HTML emails with Tailwind CSS](https://adminlte.io/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/maizzle-tailwind-email.png)

HTML + Tailwind CSS + Node.js

Free / MIT

Best for: Tailwind CSS Developers

**Why we like it:** Maizzle bridges the gap between modern web development and email. Write actual HTML with Tailwind utility classes, and the build system handles inlining styles, removing unused CSS, and generating email-client-safe output.

Unlike MJML’s custom syntax, Maizzle uses real HTML augmented with Tailwind CSS. The build process inlines styles, purges unused CSS, minifies the output, and applies email-specific optimizations. With 2.7k stars and growing, Maizzle is the best choice for teams already using Tailwind. If you’re working with Tailwind beyond email, you might also like our [Tailwind portfolio templates](https://adminlte.io/blog/tailwind-portfolio-templates/) roundup.

[GitHub](https://github.com/maizzle/maizzle) [Website](https://maizzle.com/)

## 13. email-templates
Free / MIT

Best for: Node.js Backend Email Rendering

With 3.7k stars and active maintenance through 2026, it’s the most flexible Node.js email rendering solution.

It handles CSS inlining, responsive design, and includes a browser preview feature for development.

## How to Choose the Right Approach
**Use React/JSX frameworks** (React Email, JSX Email, Mailing) when your team already works with React and you want component reuse, TypeScript safety, and a modern development experience.

MJML is the safest bet; Maizzle if you prefer Tailwind CSS.
